scope: One planning, implementation or fresh-session review phase per conversation. A task (T-nn) groups about five stories (SF-nnn), done in the listed order in one implementation conversation and reviewed as a whole in a fresh one. The default queue is the planned tasks in the order below; stretch needs the owner's explicit promotion. Story cards hold the acceptance criteria; status lives only here, per task.

status_definitions.todo: Not started; ready when every dependency is done.
status_definitions.in_progress: Implementation is active; resume before selecting another task.
status_definitions.review_required: Implementation evidence ready; needs a fresh-session review.
status_definitions.changes_requested: The review found changes; resume implementation.
status_definitions.done: Accepted by a fresh-session review with its tests passing; see production_verification separately.
status_definitions.blocked: A concrete external blocker is recorded in blocked_reason; continue other ready work.

open_decisions.question: Android packaging approach. Recommended: a Trusted Web Activity generated with Bubblewrap, wrapping the hosted PWA (smallest change; invite links keep working). Alternative: Capacitor (bundles the files; larger restructure; invite links would need rework).
open_decisions.answer: Approved: a Trusted Web Activity generated with Bubblewrap.

open_decisions.question: Android package name (permanent after the first Play upload), e.g. com.<owner>.splitsheet.
open_decisions.answer: com.splitfamilia.app. The owner doesn't want their personal name in the package (it is public in the Play URL and in the phone's app info), so the earlier com.revanparimi prefix was dropped. It can still change until SF-011 starts; it is permanent after the first Play upload. If Play reports the ID as taken at the first upload, pick another before anything ships.

open_decisions.question: App name for the store and inside the app: 'Splitsheet' (what the app shows today), 'SplitFamilia' (the repo name), or another.

open_decisions.question: Production web host: where is the app live today (GitHub Pages?), and may it move to Firebase Hosting on project splitfamilia-cf927 (recommended, because it serves /.well-known/assetlinks.json at the domain root)?
open_decisions.answer: Railway, following the StockAgent-main pattern: one Dockerfile deployed as a Railway service; the container serves the PWA at the domain root, including /.well-known/assetlinks.json. The owner creates and configures the Railway service and its domain. The owner already pays for Railway Pro (US$20/month), so hosting cost is not a constraint.

open_decisions.question: Google Play developer account type: personal or organization.
open_decisions.answer: Personal account. Note: on personal accounts Google Play shows the legal name, country and developer email publicly, and the developer display name can differ (e.g. 'SplitFamilia'). SF-002 must explain this.
